title: Redwood - Cost Econ Discovery with Palisade Capital
summary: Intro discovery focused on unit economics for text generation at Palisade Capital. Customer runs inference for research and production pipelines, target use is chat and analytics with average sequences ~480 tokens and spikes to 2k for long docs. Main questions: per-token price vs open model hosting, effectiveness of batching and KV/prefix caching to meet budget, options for dedicated/reserved capacity to lower unit costs, and security constraints (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Agreed next steps: share pricing sheet, propose pilot config, schedule technical deep dive for benchmarking and network egress discussion.
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet and example unit economics calc; due 2026-09-02
Maya Singh: Prepare recommended batching/caching profile + quantization options based on their average seq length; due 2026-09-04
Ethan Cole: Provide sample traffic pattern JSON and token distribution for two workloads; due 2026-09-03
Jordan Lee: Set up 1-week benchmark pilot on Redwood hosted and dedicated (if ok) - await customer's go-ahead; due 2026-09-07
next_steps: Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) week of Sep 7
Receive traffic sample from Palisade to size Dedicated proposal
Share SOC2 and KMS docs (private deployment notes)
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-08-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Palisade Head of ML), Priya Patel (CTO), Marcus Yu (Lead Infra), Lina Gomez (Data Scientist)

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan with Redwood Inference, with me is Maya our platform SE. Quick agenda: understand your workloads, talk unit economics — hosted vs dedicated vs private — then propose next steps.
00:18 Ethan: Thanks Jordan, yeah we've been evaluating a few options. We're curious on per-token pricing and how batching & prefix caching can reduce costs. Our main constraint is staying under roughly $25k/month for inference.
00:32 Maya: Great, can you give a quick profile of your requests? average seq length, qps, and percent long documents?
00:40 Priya: Sure, our chat queries average around 480 tokens per session, but our batch analytics jobs hit up to 2k tokens; baseline qps is 6-8 but we get spikes to 40 qps during market opens.
01:02 Marcus: Also network egress matters — we have some restrictions on cross-region traffic and prefer VPC peering for private deployments.
01:12 Jordan: Understood. So on Redwood hosted API you'd pay per-token usage — we have published per-token tiers — and you can lower per-token costs with batching and caching. On Dedicated you can buy reserved capacity which reduces unit cost for sustained throughput. On Private you get full control but there's a platform fee and infra cost.
01:33 Ethan: Do you have any back-of-envelope numbers we can use? per 1M tokens hosted vs dedicated?
01:38 Maya: Roughly speaking, across typical open models we see hosted at X cents per 1k tokens for generation; for this call I'll use an example: hosted generation around $3.50 — sorry $3.50 per 1k tokens for heavier models — which is $3,500 per million tokens; dedicated can cut that to under $2k per million depending on commit and quantization. But note these numbers vary by model family and quantization.
02:05 Lina: Sorry can I interrupt, you said kv cache and prefix caching — how much do those help for chat?
02:12 Maya: Good Q. For chat where you have a lot of repeated context, prefix caching can shave off tokens if you avoid resending static system context; KV cache benefits streaming chat, reducing compute for repeated tokens especially for long contexts. In practice we see 20-60% effective token reduction depending on how much of the prompt is repeated.
02:34 Priya: And batching? We care about latency during spikes — can batching introduce bad tail latency?
02:40 Maya: Redwood runtime uses continuous batching and can be tuned with latency SLOs. You can configure max_batch_delay and preferred batch size; we typically keep p95 latency targets by limiting batch windows. There's a tradeoff: higher batching reduces cost per token but increases p99 tail. For interactive chat we'd recommend smaller batch windows combined with KV caching; for analytics jobs you can use larger batches.
03:05 Marcus: On Dedicated — what's the typical commit for a medium team? monthly GPUs or tokens?
03:11 Jordan: Commit is usually in terms of reserved capacity (vCPU/GPU hours or inference slots) with an expected throughput figure, and we translate to expected unit cost. A mid-size commit can be e.g., 2-4 reserved A100-ish equivalents which for your workload might cover baseline qps and drop unit cost ~35-50%.
03:36 Ethan: Do you support mixed precision or quantization profiles? That matters for cost.
03:40 Maya: Yes, we support FP16, INT8 and some 4-bit quant profiles depending on model compatibility. Quantization reduces memory footprint and can significantly lower cost on Dedicated. There's a small quality delta; we'd run evals on your prompts to measure.
03:56 Priya: Security — we need SOC2, SSO, KMS for key management, and audit logs. If we go Private, we require VPC and HSM integration.
04:06 Jordan: We can share SOC2 and SSO docs. Our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations and audit logging; Hosted can integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping in some cases but Private gives you full control.
04:20 Lina: Any differences on data retention between hosted and private?
04:23 Jordan: Hosted keeps logs and transcriptions per policy; we have options to disable data retention for enterprise tiers. Private gives you full control.
04:31 Ethan: Back to costs — can you show a worked example? Say 1M generated tokens per month with avg seq 480, what's the cost across choices?
04:40 Maya: Quick example: hosted: $3,500 per 1M tokens (example heavy model) before caching/batching; if you achieve 30% effective token savings with caching and batching, that's $2,450 effective. Dedicated with a commit could be $1,800 per 1M tokens assuming 40% commit of the reserved capacity and quantized model; Private would be infra + ops but can be similar or lower at high scale. We'll run precise calc with your token distribution.
05:10 Priya: What about burst capacity? We can't have requests fail at market open.
05:15 Jordan: Hosted supports burst capacity and auto-scaling; Dedicated supports burst via configured burst pools or overflow routing to hosted; you can set fallback policies to route to hosted variants with higher cost but greater availability.
05:31 Marcus: How do you handle fallbacks when models are not identical — e.g., quantized variant vs full-fp16?
05:37 Maya: Our smart routing routes to compatible variants and we flag quality deltas. You can set automatic fallback policies with thresholds — for instance, if latency SLO is violated, route to lower-cost or alternative region.
05:49 Ethan: Any hidden costs? egress, storage, logging?
05:52 Jordan: Good to ask: egress and storage are billed separately on Dedicated/Private depending on infra. Hosted includes standard logs but long-term observability/retention is an add-on. We'll include egress assumptions in the pricing sheet.
06:10 Lina: For benchmarking — can we run a small pilot to compare hosted vs dedicated performance on our prompts?
06:16 Maya: Absolutely. Typical approach: you share sample traffic; we run a 1-week benchmark on hosted, and if you want Dedicated, we can size a trial reserved pool. We capture latency p50/p95/p99 and cost per token with caching enabled.
06:30 Priya: Timeline question — we're trying to decide by mid-September.
06:34 Jordan: That works. If you can share traffic samples this week and give the go-ahead we can start the pilot next week and have results within 7 days.
06:42 Ethan: Ok we'll do that. A few nitty-gritty questions: how are tokens counted for embeddings vs generation? We do both.
06:51 Maya: We count generation tokens for output + relevant prompt tokens for model cost. Embeddings are billed differently per embedding unit — we'll send the exact unit definitions by model.
07:02 Marcus: On-prem: if we wanted an air-gapped deployment, what's the lift?
07:07 Jordan: Private on-prem is supported but involves an installer, networking prep, and a small professional services engagement for setup and KMS/HSM integration. Typical lead time is 6-10 weeks depending on site.
07:22 Ethan: Regarding quality regressions with quantization, how do you monitor that?
07:26 Maya: We integrate eval hooks and quality monitoring in Redwood Optimize — you set test prompt sets and we alert on regression; we can also run A/B tests during rollouts.
07:40 Priya: For pricing, can you show us a few model profiles at different token volumes?
07:45 Jordan: Yes we'll send a pricing sheet with worked examples for 250k, 1M, 5M tokens/month across hosted, dedicated (with 6-month commit), and private infra estimates.
07:58 Lina: One more: do you have tooling to estimate effective token savings from caching given our chat retention patterns?
08:04 Maya: We do — if you provide sample sessions we can run a quick estimation of repeated context and expected savings; usually we present a conservative and optimistic estimate.
08:14 Ethan: Anything else we should be aware of when comparing to alternatives like OpenAI or Anthropic?
08:19 Jordan: Main differences: control and observability. OpenAI can be simpler but less flexible for dedicated/private. With Redwood you get unified APIs across modes, routing controls, and cost levers (quantization/batching/caching) that you can tune. We'll include competitor notes in the doc we send.
08:38 Marcus: On contract language — do you do SLAs for latency and uptime on Dedicated?
08:42 Jordan: Yes Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency objectives; details are in enterprise terms.
08:48 Priya: Ok let's recap next steps.
08:51 Jordan: Recap: we'll send pricing + cost calc, SOC2/KMS docs, and a proposed pilot plan. You (Ethan) will share traffic sample and token distribution. We'll schedule a SE-led deep dive next week.
08:59 Ethan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
09:02 Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with materials.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings, e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash" and Redwood product name occasionally spelled "Redwood Infer".

End of transcript.
